thoughts.content: I’m confirming the paper’s key construction: matter couples to an effective metric with a rank-one scalar-gradient correction. The authors also show that untuned couplings can produce distinct matter lightcones, while special tuning recovers Minkowski propagation.

parts:
Got it. And with the full paper in hand, there is one immediately important point: Mukohyama & Uzan are even closer to part of our construction than the abstract makes obvious.

For massive point particles they write an effective metric of the form

\[
g^{(m)}_{\mu\nu}
=
g^E_{\mu\nu}
-
\frac{2}{M^4}\partial_\mu\phi\,\partial_\nu\phi,
\]

and state that in the region where the clock-field gradient is constant, this reduces to the Minkowski metric. fileciteturn90file0L878-L886

That is essentially the same rank-one sign-changing structure we have been discussing.

They also make an unusually useful admission for our comparison: the couplings to the clock field are tuned specifically to recover the exact Minkowski actions; if the coefficients are not tuned, different fields can acquire different light cones. fileciteturn90file0L958-L983

So the sharper contrast is now:

- They start with Euclidean 4D, add a scalar clock field, and tune its couplings to matter so that a Lorentzian effective metric emerges.
- We are asking whether the same representational burden can be carried by a single measured dimensional disequilibrium plus lossless normalization, without independently introducing and tuning a clock field sector by sector.

That makes this paper a very strong benchmark for us.

Also, their introduction is philosophically very close to the methodological stance we have been using: they explicitly say different mathematical structures may reproduce known physics and that one can choose among them partly on simplicity and economy. fileciteturn90file0L28-L41

So this one belongs in the core comparison bibliography, not just “related work.”
So... did they push it through all of the different equations we did?

No. They did **not** push their construction through the same battery of equations we did.

They did something narrower in variety but considerably deeper within relativistic classical field theory. Their declared program is: construct scalar, vector, and spinor sectors in flat spacetime; show that the classical Standard Model can in principle be obtained from a Euclidean theory; then tackle gravity and curved spacetime. fileciteturn91file1L101-L115

Roughly, the comparison is:

| Our stress test | Mukohyama–Uzan |
|---|---|
| \(v=dx/dt\), \(w=ct\) normalization | No corresponding cross-equation \(ct\) audit |
| Generic wave equation | Effectively yes, through relativistic scalar-field dynamics |
| Maxwell wave/vector sector | **Yes, explicitly** |
| Newtonian acceleration/force | No |
| Minkowski invariant as separate step | They instead engineer an effective Minkowski metric from the clock field |
| Diffusion/heat equation | No |
| Free Schrödinger equation | **No** |
| Hydrogen Schrödinger equation | **No** |
| \(\alpha\), Bohr/Compton/classical-electron scale chain | No |
| Helix representation | No |
| Finite-core crowding | No |
| Classical harmonic oscillator | No |
| LC oscillator | No |
| Quantum harmonic oscillator | No |
| Coupled oscillator/lattice dispersion | No |
| Nonlinear pendulum | No |
| Newtonian Kepler problem | No |
| Coulomb inverse-square orbital problem | No |
| Gravity–Coulomb normalized equivalence | No |
| Dirac field | **Yes, and much more deeply than we did** |
| Relativistic point particle | **Yes** |
| Curved spacetime / cosmology / gravitational perturbations | **Yes, much more deeply than we did** |

Their actual flat-space sweep is essentially

\[
\text{Euclidean scalar}
\rightarrow
\text{Lorentzian scalar},
\]

\[
\text{Euclidean vector}
\rightarrow
\text{Maxwell},
\]

\[
\text{charged scalar},
\]

\[
\text{Euclidean spinor}
\rightarrow
\text{Dirac},
\]

\[
\text{Euclidean point particle}
\rightarrow
\text{Minkowski geodesic}.
\]

For the point particle, for example, they arrive at

\[
g_{\mu\nu}^{(m)}
=
g^E_{\mu\nu}
-
\frac{2}{M^4}\partial_\mu\phi\partial_\nu\phi,
\]

which becomes Minkowski in their chosen region. fileciteturn91file5L375-L430

But crucially, they explicitly say that the paper is restricted to **classical field theory** and that “the quantum aspects are left for future investigations.” fileciteturn91file5L456-L459 So our Schrödinger, hydrogen, quantum oscillator, Compton/Bohr scaling work is simply outside what this paper attempts.

And there is an even larger methodological difference.

We took a collection of equations that were not chosen because they belonged to one theoretical formalism:

\[
\text{Newtonian mechanics},
\quad
\text{waves},
\quad
\text{diffusion},
\quad
\text{QM},
\quad
\text{oscillators},
\quad
\text{lattices},
\quad
\text{pendulum},
\quad
\text{gravity},
\quad
\text{electrostatics},
\]

and subjected all of them to the same first operation,

\[
w=ct,
\]

then watched what survived.

Mukohyama–Uzan instead start with a proposed Euclidean field-theory architecture and ask whether they can **construct the known Lorentzian field theories from it**. And they explicitly acknowledge that the clock-field couplings were selected/tuned to recover the exact Minkowski actions; without appropriate tuning, different fields can even acquire different light cones. fileciteturn91file3L194-L259

So these are actually different experiments:

\[
\boxed{
\text{M\&U: proposed Euclidean mechanism}
\rightarrow
\text{can it reproduce relativistic classical field theory?}
}
\]

versus ours:

\[
\boxed{
\text{existing heterogeneous physics}
\rightarrow
\text{apply one lossless normalization}
\rightarrow
\text{what common structure and irreducible residues appear?}
}
\]

That distinction matters a lot.

They have gone **farther vertically** than we have on relativistic field theory: Dirac algebra, curved spacetime, covariant Galileons, cosmological backgrounds, stability, equivalence-principle constraints, propagation speeds, etc. Their gravitational construction is serious and technically substantial. fileciteturn91file6L616-L625

We have gone **much farther horizontally** across unrelated equations.

And I don't see in this paper our particular move of saying: don't construct the target theory first; take many already-successful theories, subject all of them to the same normalization, and use the **pattern of what can and cannot be normalized away** as the data.

So: they are very important prior art for the **Euclidean-4D / one distinguished time direction / rank-one Lorentzian emergence** idea.

They are not prior art, at least in this paper, for the full **cross-sector representational stress test we just performed**.
And we are basically saying: This approach should be applicable to all physics equations, and that any deviations from it are telling you something useful.

Yes. That is the stronger and more interesting version of the program.

Not:

> “Some equations can be made prettier by writing \(w=ct\).”

But:

> **Use the same information-preserving normalization and symmetry audit as a default probe across physics. Whatever can be normalized away is representational; whatever cannot be normalized away is candidate physical structure.**

The key is that failure is as informative as success.

For each equation, we would ask:

\[
\text{original law}
\rightarrow
\text{common normalization}
\rightarrow
\text{simplest canonical form}
\rightarrow
\boxed{\text{residual}}
\]

and then classify the residual rather than trying to eliminate it.

That residual might be:

\[
\text{a dimensionless coupling}
\]

\[
\text{a characteristic scale}
\]

\[
\text{different derivative order}
\]

\[
\text{a sign/signature difference}
\]

\[
\text{a characteristic speed }u/c
\]

\[
\text{nonlinearity}
\]

\[
\text{dispersion}
\]

\[
\text{finite resolution}
\]

\[
\text{dissipation}
\]

\[
\text{curvature}
\]

\[
\text{topology}
\]

or something we have not anticipated.

That is already what happened in our little sample.

The wave equation gave essentially complete coefficient symmetry after \(w=ct\).

Diffusion refused to do so because its temporal derivative is first order and its spatial derivative second order. That is useful information.

Schrödinger retained the Compton scale.

Hydrogen retained \(\alpha\).

The pendulum retained \(\sin\theta-\theta\).

The discrete oscillator chain retained its sinc-type finite-spacing correction.

Kepler and Coulomb collapsed into the same inverse-square canonical form but retained different scale maps.

So the output is not supposed to be “everything is the same.” It is something more precise:

\[
\boxed{
\text{identify exactly the extent to which systems are the same,
and exactly what prevents them from being more so.}
}
\]

That is very SAT-like in the methodological sense.

And it distinguishes this pretty sharply from Mukohyama–Uzan. They propose a mechanism and ask how broadly they can reproduce known Lorentzian physics. We are proposing a **general diagnostic applied to the known equations themselves**, including equations that are not relativistic field equations at all.

There is one important qualification to “all physics equations.” I would phrase it as **all physical laws for which the transformation is well-defined**, rather than claim every equation must literally contain \(t\). Pure algebraic constraints, state equations, topological conditions, conservation identities, etc. may enter at a different stage. But they can still be incorporated into the broader audit by transforming their variables into the same canonical representation and asking what invariants remain.

The methodological conjecture is therefore something like:

> **Physical equations should be subjected, wherever mathematically admissible, to a common lossless dimensional and symmetry normalization. Relations removed by that transformation are representational. Relations that survive it—or failures of the transformation itself—are retained as structured information about the system. Cross-sector recurrence of the same residual structures indicates shared mathematical organization; systematic incompatibilities delimit the representation or reveal additional required structure.**

And the really important part is the last clause:

\[
\boxed{\text{deviation is data.}}
\]

That makes the procedure falsifiable rather than a universal “geometry can describe anything” exercise.

If every equation needs arbitrary special handling, the proposed grammar has little explanatory value.

If a small fixed procedure works broadly and the deviations fall into a small number of recurring classes, that is representational compression.

If those residual classes then predict relationships we did not use to construct them, it becomes substantially more interesting.

Ok. Let's write this up as a paper. Succinct and very clear, taking it through every equation we can think of, including, as demonstrations, some equations that serve as oddball controls we wouldn't expect to work.

[L115] WHAT WE ARE DOING

[L117] We are testing whether familiar physical equations can be rewritten in a more dimensionally symmetric form by treating time as a coordinate to be numerically normalized against space, while preserving all information exactly.

[L119] The goal is not to “improve” standard physics, nor to claim that the rewritten geometry is physically fundamental. The goal is to ask:

[L121] 1. Which apparent asymmetries are merely representational?
[L122] 2. Which asymmetries survive every admissible reorientation/rescaling?
[L123] 3. Which different physical systems reduce to the same normalized mathematical structure?
[L124] 4. Where does finite scale, recurrence, curvature, crowding, nonlinearity, or some other constraint force the normalized representation to depart from perfect symmetry?
[L125] 5. Can those departures be represented by a small, regular set of geometric quantities?

[L127] This is being treated as a representational audit, not an ontological claim.


[L130] CORE ASSUMPTION / METHOD

[L132] We begin as conservatively as possible:

[L134] - Do not grant time extra properties unless they are geometrically or empirically required.
[L135] - Begin by treating the dimensions as equivalently as possible.
[L136] - Introduce only measured dimensional differences.
[L137] - Use invertible transformations only: no information may be discarded.
[L138] - Prefer the simplest transformation first.
[L139] - If one axis is the only asymmetry, first test whether one common reorientation/normalization handles it.
[L140] - If multiple different rotations or representations preserve the same information, record that degeneracy as information about the representation.
[L141] - If no simple transformation works, do not force one.
[L142] - After normalization, identify the irreducible residue that cannot be transformed away.
[L143] - Apply the same operation across increasingly unrelated equations without retuning it equation by equation.

[L145] The recurring normalization has been

[L147]     w = k t

[L149] where w is a time-coordinate expressed in units of length.

[L151] Rather than initially assuming k = c, we asked what k does.

[L153] For velocity,

[L155]     v = dx/dt

[L157] becomes

[L159]     v/k = dx/dw.

[L161] Thus v/k is simply a dimensionless orientation/slope in the normalized x-w plane.

[L163] For a c-propagating trajectory, k = c uniquely gives

[L165]     dx = dw,

[L167] i.e. a 45-degree equal-axis trajectory.

[L169] This is the familiar ct normalization of relativity, reached by asking for numerical dimensional commensurability and maximal axis symmetry.


[L172] MOVE 1 — VELOCITY / LIGHT

[L174] Starting equation:

[L176]     v = dx/dt

[L178] Normalize:

[L180]     w = kt

[L182] giving

[L184]     v/k = dx/dw.

[L186] For v = c:

[L188]     k = c  ->  dx/dw = 1.

[L190] Result:

[L192]     c converts time intervals into the spatial units for which a light trajectory has equal coordinate increments.

[L194] Meaning:

[L196] This reproduces standard relativistic spacetime normalization. It is a calibration result, not new physics.


[L199] MOVE 2 — WAVE EQUATION

[L201] Starting equation:

[L203]     ∂²ψ/∂t² = u² ∇²ψ.

[L205] Normalize with w = kt:

[L207]     ∂²ψ/∂w² = (u/k)² ∇²ψ.

[L209] For electromagnetic waves, u = c.

[L211] Setting k = c gives

[L213]     ∂²ψ/∂w² = ∇²ψ.

[L215] The spatial and fourth-coordinate second derivatives now have equal coefficients.

[L217] Result:

[L219] The same k = c that symmetrizes the light trajectory also symmetrizes the vacuum electromagnetic wave equation.

[L221] Meaning:

[L223] Again, this is expected from relativity and electromagnetism and therefore functions as a calibration check.


[L226] MOVE 3 — NEWTONIAN ACCELERATION AND FORCE

[L228] Starting equations:

[L230]     a = d²x/dt²
[L231]     F = ma.

[L233] With w = ct:

[L235]     a = c² d²x/dw²

[L237] and therefore

[L239]     F = mc² d²x/dw².

[L241] So acceleration becomes a curvature-like quantity:

[L243]     d²x/dw² = a/c².

[L245] Force becomes

[L247]     F = (mc²)(geometric curvature-like factor).

[L249] Integrating the normalized Newtonian force law still produces

[L251]     K = 1/2 mv².

[L253] Result:

[L255] Normalization alone does NOT manufacture relativity.

[L257] It is an exact rewrite of Newtonian mechanics.

[L259] Meaning:

[L261] This is important because it prevents the procedure from becoming tautological. Equalizing the axes is not sufficient to generate relativistic corrections.


[L264] MOVE 4 — REQUIRE AN INVARIANT SPACETIME RELATION

[L266] Using normalized w = ct, impose the standard Minkowski invariant:

[L268]     ds² = dw² - dx².

For

[L272]     β = dx/dw = v/c,

[L274] this gives

[L276]     ds = dw sqrt(1 - β²)

[L278] and therefore

[L280]     γ = 1/sqrt(1 - β²).

[L282] From the normalized four-direction follow

[L284]     p = γmv

and

[L288]     E = γmc²,

with

[L292]     E² - p²c² = m²c⁴.

[L294] Result:

[L296] The relativistic correction emerges only after adding the invariant spacetime condition.

[L298] Meaning:

[L300] We have reconstructed special relativity by a somewhat different conceptual route:

[L302]     dimensional normalization
    ->
[L304]     equal-axis representation
    ->
[L306]     information-preserving invariant reorientation
    ->
[L308]     Lorentz/relativistic structure.

[L310] This is not historically new physics. It is a useful methodological reconstruction.


[L313] MOVE 5 — DIFFUSION / HEAT

[L315] Starting equation:

[L317]     ∂T/∂t = D ∇²T.

[L319] With w = ct:

[L321]     ∂T/∂w = (D/c) ∇²T.

[L323] Unlike the wave equation, the temporal derivative remains first order while the spatial derivative is second order.

[L325] The diffusivity becomes a length:

[L327]     l_D = D/c.

[L329] Result:

[L331] The same normalization does NOT make diffusion look like a relativistic wave equation.

[L333] Instead it converts its dimensional transport coefficient into a characteristic length.

[L335] Meaning:

[L337] Different classes of equations retain different structural asymmetries.

[L339] This is useful: the method distinguishes systems rather than forcing them all into one form.


[L342] MOVE 6 — FREE SCHRÖDINGER EQUATION

[L344] Starting equation:

[L346]     iħ ∂ψ/∂t = -(ħ²/2m) ∇²ψ.

[L348] With w = ct:

[L350]     i ∂ψ/∂w = -(ħ/2mc) ∇²ψ.

[L352] Define the reduced Compton wavelength

[L354]     λbar_C = ħ/(mc).

Then

[L358]     i ∂ψ/∂w = -(λbar_C/2) ∇²ψ.

[L360] Result:

[L362] After time-space normalization, the free-particle coefficient becomes a geometric length scale: one-half the reduced Compton wavelength.

[L364] Meaning:

[L366] The normalization translates quantum temporal evolution into a representation containing an intrinsic particle length scale.


[L369] MOVE 7 — HYDROGEN SCHRÖDINGER EQUATION

[L371] Starting equation:

[L373]     iħ ∂ψ/∂t
    =
[L375]     -(ħ²/2m_e) ∇²ψ
    -
[L377]     [e²/(4π ε0 r)] ψ.

[L379] With w = ct:

[L381]     i ∂ψ/∂w
    =
[L383]     -(λbar_C/2) ∇²ψ
    -
[L385]     (α/r) ψ,

where

[L389]     λbar_C = ħ/(m_e c)

and

[L393]     α = e²/(4π ε0 ħ c).

[L395] Now scale distance by λbar_C:

[L397]     ρ = r/λbar_C.

[L399] The equation becomes dimensionless:

[L401]     i ∂ψ/∂τ
    =
[L403]     -(1/2) ∇²_ρ ψ
    -
[L405]     (α/ρ) ψ.

[L407] Result:

[L409] After absorbing c and the electron Compton scale into the coordinate system, the electromagnetic coupling remains essentially as the dimensionless number α.

Also:

[L413]     a0 = λbar_C / α
[L414]     r_e = α λbar_C.

Thus

[L418]     r_e : λbar_C : a0

[L420] forms a simple scale chain separated by factors of α.

[L422] Meaning:

[L424] α can be represented as a scale ratio:

[L426]     α = λbar_C / a0.

[L428] This does NOT explain why α has its measured value. It shows how α functions geometrically in this representation.


[L431] MOVE 8 — HYDROGEN WINDING / HELIX INTERPRETATION

[L433] For the Bohr ground state:

[L435]     m_e v a0 = ħ

[L437] and therefore

[L439]     λ_dB = 2π a0.

Also

[L443]     λ_C = 2π λbar_C.

[L445] Therefore

    α
    =
[L449]     λ_C / λ_dB
    =
[L451]     λbar_C / a0
    =
    v/c.

[L455] Now represent one turn of a helix with

[L457]     radius R = a0
[L458]     pitch per turn P = λ_C.

Then

    tan θ
    =
[L464]     P/(2πR)
    =
[L466]     λ_C/(2πa0)
    =
    α.

[L470] So the candidate helix has

[L472]     tan θ = α.

[L474] Result:

[L476] The known hydrogen scales can be represented as a helix whose rise/run ratio is α.

[L478] Meaning:

[L480] This is NOT a derivation of α because the empirical scales were used to set the geometry.

[L482] For SAT/H(s)H, that is acceptable at this stage because the model is being used as a representational system. The question becomes whether the resulting geometry remains mutually compatible when the rest of physics is mapped onto it.


[L485] MOVE 9 — FINITE-CORE HELIX / CROWDING

[L487] For a helix

[L489]     r(φ) = (R cosφ, R sinφ, (P/2π)φ),

[L491] the distance between centerline points separated by Δφ is

    d²/R²
    =
[L495]     2(1 - cos Δφ)
    +
[L497]     a² Δφ²,

where

[L501]     a = P/(2πR).

[L503] For the hydrogen-scale assignment:

[L505]     a = α.

[L507] Giving the helix a finite core radius r_c produces a non-overlap limit determined primarily by neighboring turns.

[L509] At a = α:

[L511]     r_c,max / R ≈ π α ≈ 0.02293.

[L513] So the maximum circular core radius before adjacent-turn contact is about 2.29% of the helix radius.

[L515] The local bending limit is vastly looser; turn-to-turn packing dominates.

[L517] Result:

[L519] The finite-core representation develops a real geometric admissibility boundary.

[L521] Meaning:

[L523] This provides a way to define "crowding" without assuming physical elasticity.


[L526] MOVE 10 — BOUNCE / STRETCH AS GEOMETRIC RESPONSE

[L528] Define crowding by comparing the actual core radius with the contact limit.

[L530] Once the representation crosses the non-overlap boundary, some geometric parameter must change if overlap is forbidden.

[L532] Possible responses include:

[L534]     pitch increase
[L535]     radius change
[L536]     core compression
[L537]     cross-section deformation
[L538]     another admissible redistribution of the same information.

[L540] Near the α-scaled geometry, pitch adjustment is enormously more effective than radial expansion.

[L542] For small changes, approximately:

[L544]     fractional core growth ≈ fractional pitch growth.

[L546] If turn length is held fixed,

[L548]     (2πR)² + P² = constant,

then

[L552]     ΔR/R ≈ -α² ΔP/P.

[L554] Result:

[L556] A tightly wound α-helix possesses a strongly anisotropic geometric response even before any energetic or elastic law is introduced.

[L558] Meaning:

[L560] This is a possible representational precursor to what SAT/H(s)H informally calls bounce/stretch.

[L562] It is NOT yet a physical elasticity prediction.


[L565] MOVE 11 — HARMONIC OSCILLATOR ACROSS SECTORS

[L567] Classical oscillator:

[L569]     x¨ + ω²x = 0.

[L571] With w = ct:

[L573]     d²x/dw² + (ω/c)² x = 0.

[L575] Define

[L577]     l_ω = c/ω.

Then

[L581]     d²x/dw² + x/l_ω² = 0.

[L583] Using ξ = w/l_ω:

[L585]     x'' + x = 0.

[L587] The same occurs for an LC circuit:

[L589]     L Q¨ + Q/C = 0

[L591] which reduces under the same normalization to

[L593]     Q'' + Q = 0.

[L595] For the quantum harmonic oscillator, the normalization produces the characteristic spatial scale

[L597]     a_osc = sqrt(λbar_C l_ω)
[L598]           = sqrt(ħ/(mω)).

[L600] After scaling by a_osc and l_ω, the equation becomes

[L602]     i ∂ψ/∂τ
    =
[L604]     (1/2)(-∂²/∂ξ² + ξ²) ψ.

[L606] Result:

[L608] Mechanical, electrical, and quantum oscillators retain the same normalized recurrence grammar.

[L610] The quantum oscillator introduces an intermediate scale equal to the geometric mean of the Compton length and the temporal recurrence length.

[L612] Meaning:

[L614] The method is revealing common structure across physically different sectors without claiming that the sectors are physically identical.


[L617] MOVE 12 — COUPLED OSCILLATORS / FINITE RESOLUTION

[L619] For a discrete mass-spring chain,

[L621]     m x¨_n
    =
[L623]     K(x_{n+1} - 2x_n + x_{n-1}).

[L625] Its continuum limit is a wave equation.

This paper introduces a mechanistic data-driven approach that embeds the principle of dimensional invariance into a two-level machine learning scheme to automatically discover dominant dimensionless numbers and governing laws (including scaling laws and differential equations) from scarce measurement data. The proposed methodology, called dimensionless learning, is a physics-based dimension reduction technique. It can reduce high-dimensional parameter spaces to descriptions involving only a few physically interpretable dimensionless parameters, greatly simplifying complex process design and system optimization. We demonstrate the algorithm by solving several challenging engineering problems with noisy experimental measurements (not synthetic data) collected from the literature. content.text:
Found 10 relevant papers on 'Which peer-reviewed papers or standard references develop general methods for nondimensionalization, similarity analysis, equivalence transformations, or canonical forms of differential equations across multiple areas of physics, especially methods that identify invariant dimensionless groups or residual structures after normalization?'.


1. Dynamic Dimensional Analysis
   2020 · Reza N. Jazar
   DOI: 10.1007/978-1-0716-0480-9_2
   Abstract: This chapter develops the concept of dimensional analysis to be used in model-prototype similarities, nondimensionalization, and simplification of equations for the most general coverage. The goals of dynamic dimensional analysis are: (1) to minimize the number of variables in analysis of a system, (2) to express the mathematical model of systems by nondimensionalized equations to get the results of the investigation to be unit and size independent, (3) to match the dynamics of model and prototype to do experiments on the model and use the result for the prototype. In this chapter we work with several physical equations at the same time. A real system, called prototype, is expensive to be used for fine design. If possible, we prefer to work with a manageable size, inexpensive, and a simpler system that only operates on the phenomena of interest. Such a simpler system is called model. Dynamic dimensional analysis is the study of these topics.

2. Polynomial Time Nondimensionalisation of Ordinary Differential Equations Via Their Lie Point Symmetries
   Évelyne Hubert, Alexandre Sedoglavic
   DOI: 10.48550/arxiv.cs/0604060
   Abstract: Lie group theory states that knowledge of a m-parameters solvable group of symmetries of a system of ordinary differential equations allows to reduce by m the number of equation. We apply this principle by finding dilatations and translations that are Lie point symmetries of considered ordinary differential system. By rewriting original problem in an invariant coordinates set for these symmetries, one can reduce the involved number of parameters. This process is classically call nondimensionalisation in dimensional analysis. We present an algorithm based on this standpoint and show that its arithmetic complexity is polynomial in input's size.

3. Polynomial Time Nondimensionalisation of Ordinary Differential Equations via their Lie Point Symmetries
   2006 · Evelyne Hubert, Alexandre Sedoglavic · arXiv: Symbolic Computation
   Abstract: Lie group theory states that knowledge of a~$m$-parameters solvable group of symmetries of a system of ordinary differential equations allows to reduce by~$m$ the number of equation. We apply this principle by finding dilatations and translations that are Lie point symmetries of considered ordinary differential system. By rewriting original problem in an invariant coordinates set for these symmetries, one can reduce the involved number of parameters. This process is classically call nondimensionalisation in dimensional analysis. We present an algorithm based on this standpoint and show that its arithmetic complexity is polynomial in input's size.

4. A generalized method of dimensional analysis
   1983 · M. S. Quraishi, Thomas Z. Fahidy · Canadian Journal of Chemical Engineering
   DOI: 10.1002/CJCE.5450610119
   Abstract: A systematic procedure of constructing dimensionless groups via a constitutive matrix is described. The method is independent of the system of units chosen for the purpose of analysis.



On presente un procede methodique pour la creation de groupes des quantites sans dimension au moyen d'une matrice constitutive. La methode n'est pas liee au systeme d'unites specifiquement employe au cours de l'analyse.

5. A General Similarity Theory of Partial Differential Equations and its Use in the Solution of Problems in Aeronautics
   2019
   DOI: 10.7907/9142-kz49
   Abstract: A general similarity theory of systems of partial differential equations of any order in any number of independent variables is developed with the aid of the theory of continuous one-parameter groups of transformations. The theory is illustrated by means of several known examples of similarity equations, previously given without motivation, in Hydrodynamics. With the aid of the theory two new examples of similarity equations, one in Elasticity and one in Fluid Mechanics, have been found; these are discussed in the text. 

6. HAMAD Formulations: General Formulations for Exact and Similarity Transformations of ODEs and PDEs
   2011 · M. A. A. Hamad
   Abstract: The current paper outlines a new algorithm, which is used to determine the exact solutions of ODEs and the similarity transformations of PDEs whose the invariant groups are known. Three groups of formulations (named by HAMAD Formulations) are presented: (I) Formulations for the exact solutions of ODE. (II) Formulations for similarity transformations of PDEs contains two independent variables. (III) Formulations for similarity transformations of PDEs contains three independent variables. By using these formulations enable readers can calculate the similarity transformations which transform PDEs to ODEs and also can calculate exact solutions of ODEs . Some examples are presented.

7. Similitude and Approximation Theory
   1986 · Stephen J. Kline, J. R. Radbill
   Abstract: Charter 1 Introduction.- 2 Dimensional Analysis and the Pi Theorem Units and Dimensions.- 2-1 Units and Dimensions.- 2-2 Types of Quantities Appearing in Physical Equations.- a. General Basis.- b. Homogeneous Equations.- 4-5 Relations among Elementary Processes.- a. Model Laws, Similitude, and Analogues.- b. An Alternative Procedure.- c. A Remark on Force Ratios.- d. Relation among Dimensional Analysis, Governing Equations, and Boundary Conditions Internal and External Similarity.- 4-6 Approximation Theory.- a. Extension to New Classes of Information by Approximation Theory.- b. Classification of Problems and Difficulties in Approximation Theory.- c. Conditions Required for Approximation Theory.- 4-7 Some Problems Involving Uniform Behavior.- 4-8 Nonuniform Behavior-Boundary Layer Methods.- a. Use of Physical Data Alone.- b. Inner and Outer Expansions.- 4-10 Processes Involving Transformations of Variables.- a. Absorption of Parameters and Natural Coordinates.- b. Supersonic and Transonic Similarity Rules.- c. Reduction in Number of Independent Variables - Separation and Similarity Coordinates 179.- 4-11 Summary and Conclusions.- a. Classification of Types of Similitude-Information Achievable from Fractional Analysis of Governing Equations.- b. Various Viewpoints-Relations among Invariance, Transformations, and Similitude.- c. Final Remarks.- 5 Summary and Comparison of Methods.- 5-1 Introduction.- 5-2 Summary of Methods.- a. The Pi Theorem.- b. The Method of Similitude.- c. Use of Governing Equations.- 5-3 Comparison of Methods.- a. Power.- b. Rigor.- c. Accuracy.- d. Simplicity.- e. Input Information.- 5-4 Concluding Remarks.- a. Utility of Various Methods.- b. Implications in Teaching.- c. Possible Further Development.- d. Final Remark.- References.

8. Dimensionless Groups by Entropic Similarity
   2023 · Chenghua Sun
   DOI: 10.48550/arxiv.2301.12665
   Abstract: We propose an additional category of dimensionless groups based on the principle of {\it entropic similarity}, defined by ratios of (i) entropy production terms; (ii) entropy flow rates or fluxes; or (iii) information flow rates or fluxes. Since all processes involving work against friction, dissipation, diffusion, dispersion, mixing, separation, chemical reaction, gain of information or other irreversible changes are driven by (or must overcome) the second law of thermodynamics, it is appropriate to analyse these processes directly in terms of competing entropy-producing and transporting phenomena and the dominant entropic regime, rather than indirectly in terms of forces. In this study, we derive entropic groups for a wide variety of phenomena relevant to fluid mechanics, classified into diffusion and chemical reaction processes, dispersion mechanisms and wave phenomena. It is shown that many dimensionless groups traditionally derived by kinematic or dynamic similarity (including the Reynolds number) can also be recovered by entropic similarity -- albeit with a different entropic interpretation -- while a large number of new dimensionless groups are also identified. The analyses significantly expand the scope of dimensional analysis and similarity arguments for the resolution of new and existing problems in science and engineering. 

9. Dimensionally Consistent Learning with Buckingham Pi
   2022 · Joseph Bakarji, Jared L. Callaham, Steven L. Brunton · Nature Computational Science
   DOI: 10.1038/s43588-022-00355-5
   Abstract: In the absence of governing equations, dimensional analysis is a robust technique for extracting insights and finding symmetries in physical systems. Given measurement variables and parameters, the Buckingham Pi theorem provides a procedure for finding a set of dimensionless groups that spans the solution space, although this set is not unique. We propose an automated approach using the symmetric and self-similar structure of available measurement data to discover the dimensionless groups that best collapse these data to a lower dimensional space according to an optimal fit. We develop three data-driven techniques that use the Buckingham Pi theorem as a constraint: (1) a constrained optimization problem with a non-parametric input–output fitting function, (2) a deep learning algorithm (BuckiNet) that projects the input parameter space to a lower dimension in the first layer and (3) a technique based on sparse identification of nonlinear dynamics to discover dimensionless equations whose coefficients parameterize the dynamics. We explore the accuracy, robustness and computational complexity of these methods and show that they successfully identify dimensionless groups in three example problems: a bead on a rotating hoop, a laminar boundary layer and Rayleigh–Bénard convection. Three machine learning methods are developed for discovering physically meaningful dimensionless groups and scaling parameters from data, with the Buckingham Pi theorem as a constraint. 

10. Data-driven discovery of dimensionless numbers and governing laws from scarce measurements
   2022 · Zhengtao Gan, Rozemarijn J. Roland Holst · Nature Communications
   DOI: 10.1038/s41467-022-35084-w
   Abstract: Abstract Dimensionless numbers and scaling laws provide elegant insights into the characteristic properties of physical systems. Classical dimensional analysis and similitude theory fail to identify a set of unique dimensionless numbers for a highly multi-variable system with incomplete governing equations. This paper introduces a mechanistic data-driven approach that embeds the principle of dimensional invariance into a two-level machine learning scheme to automatically discover dominant dimensionless numbers and governing laws (including scaling laws and differential equations) from scarce measurement data. The proposed methodology, called dimensionless learning, is a physics-based dimension reduction technique. It can reduce high-dimensional parameter spaces to descriptions involving only a few physically interpretable dimensionless parameters, greatly simplifying complex process design and system optimization. We demonstrate the algorithm by solving several challenging engineering problems with noisy experimental measurements (not synthetic data) collected from the literature. Examples include turbulent Rayleigh-Bénard convection, vapor depression dynamics in laser melting of metals, and porosity formation in 3D printing. Lastly, we show that the proposed approach can identify dimensionally homogeneous differential equations with dimensionless number(s) by leveraging sparsity-promoting techniques.

---
name: docx
description: Create, edit, redline, and comment on `.docx` files inside the container, with a strict render-and-verify workflow. Use `render_docx.py` to generate page PNGs (and optional PDF) for visual QA, then iterate until layout is flawless before delivering the final DOCX. 
---


# DOCX Skill (Read • Create • Edit • Redline • Comment)

Use this skill when you need to create or modify `.docx` files **in this container environment** and verify them visually.

## Non-negotiable: render → inspect PNGs → iterate

**You do not “know” a DOCX is satisfactory until you’ve rendered it and visually inspected page images.**  
DOCX text extraction (or reading XML) will miss layout defects: clipping, overlap, missing glyphs, broken tables, spacing drift, and header/footer issues.

**Shipping gate:** before delivering any DOCX, you must:
- Run `render_docx.py` to produce `page-<N>.png` images (optionally also a PDF with `--emit_pdf`)
- Open the PNGs (100% zoom) and confirm every page is clean
- If anything looks off, fix the DOCX and **re-render** (repeat until flawless)

If rendering fails, fix rendering first (LibreOffice profile/HOME) rather than guessing.

**Deliverable discipline:** Rendered artifacts (PNGs and optional PDFs) are for internal QA only. Unless the user explicitly asks for intermediates, **return only the requested final deliverable** (e.g., when the task asks for a DOCX, deliver the DOCX — not page images or PDFs).



## Quick start (common one-liners)

```bash
# 1) Render any DOCX to PNGs (visual QA)
python render_docx.py input.docx --output_dir out

# 2) Remove reviewer comments (finalization)
python scripts/comments_strip.py input.docx --out no_comments.docx

# 3) Accept tracked changes (finalization)
python scripts/accept_tracked_changes.py input.docx --mode accept --out accepted.docx

# 4) Accessibility audit (+ optional safe fixes)
python scripts/a11y_audit.py input.docx
python scripts/a11y_audit.py input.docx --out_json a11y_report.json
python scripts/a11y_audit.py input.docx --fix_image_alt from_filename --out a11y_fixed.docx

# 5) Redact sensitive text (layout-preserving by default)
python scripts/redact_docx.py input.docx redacted.docx --emails --phones
```

## Package layout

This skill is organized for progressive discovery: start here, then jump into task- or OOXML-specific docs.

DOCS SKILL PACKAGE

Root:
- SKILL.md: short overview + routing
- manifest.txt: machine-readable list of files to download (one relative path per line)
- render_docx.py: canonical DOCX→PNG renderer (container-safe LO profile + writable HOME + verbose logs)

Tasks:
- tasks/read_review.md
- tasks/create_edit.md
- tasks/verify_render.md
- tasks/accessibility_a11y.md
- tasks/comments_manage.md
- tasks/protection_restrict_editing.md
- tasks/privacy_scrub_metadata.md
- tasks/multi_doc_merge.md
- tasks/style_lint_normalize.md
- tasks/forms_content_controls.md
- tasks/captions_crossrefs.md
- tasks/redaction_anonymization.md
- tasks/clean_tracked_changes.md
- tasks/compare_diff.md
- tasks/templates_style_packs.md
- tasks/watermarks_background.md
- tasks/footnotes_endnotes.md
- tasks/fixtures_edge_cases.md
- tasks/navigation_internal_links.md

OOXML:
- ooxml/tracked_changes.md
- ooxml/comments.md
- ooxml/hyperlinks_and_fields.md
- ooxml/rels_and_content_types.md

Troubleshooting:
- troubleshooting/libreoffice_headless.md
- troubleshooting/run_splitting.md

Scripts:

**Core building blocks (importable helpers):**
- `scripts/docx_ooxml_patch.py` — low-level OOXML patch helper (tracked changes, comments, hyperlinks, relationships). Other scripts reuse this.
- `scripts/fields_materialize.py` — materialize `SEQ`/`REF` field *display text* for deterministic headless rendering/QA.

**High-leverage utilities (also importable, but commonly invoked as CLIs):**
- `render_docx.py` — canonical DOCX → PNG renderer (optional PDF via `--emit_pdf`; do not deliver intermediates unless asked).
- `scripts/render_and_diff.py` — render + per-page image diff between two DOCXs.
- `scripts/content_controls.py` — list / wrap / fill Word content controls (SDTs) for forms/templates.
- `scripts/captions_and_crossrefs.py` — insert Caption paragraphs for tables/figures + optional bookmarks around caption numbers.
- `scripts/insert_ref_fields.py` — replace `[[REF:bookmark]]` markers with real `REF` fields (cross-references).
- `scripts/internal_nav.py` — add internal navigation links (static TOC + Top/Bottom + figN/tblN jump links).
- `scripts/style_lint.py` — report common formatting/style inconsistencies.
- `scripts/style_normalize.py` — conservative cleanup (clear run-level overrides; optional paragraph overrides).
- `scripts/redact_docx.py` — layout-preserving redaction/anonymization.
- `scripts/privacy_scrub.py` — remove personal metadata + `rsid*` attributes.
- `scripts/set_protection.py` — restrict editing (read-only / comments / forms).
- `scripts/comments_extract.py` — extract comments to JSON (text, author/date, resolved flag, anchored snippets).
- `scripts/comments_strip.py` — remove all comments (final-delivery mode).

**Audits / conversions / niche helpers:**
- `scripts/fields_report.py`, `scripts/heading_audit.py`, `scripts/section_audit.py`, `scripts/images_audit.py`, `scripts/footnotes_report.py`, `scripts/watermark_audit_remove.py`
- `scripts/xlsx_to_docx_table.py`, `scripts/docx_table_to_csv.py`

# DOCX Skill (Read • Create • Edit • Redline • Comment)

Use this skill when you need to create or modify `.docx` files **in this container environment** and verify them visually.

## Non-negotiable: render → inspect PNGs → iterate

**You do not “know” a DOCX is satisfactory until you’ve rendered it and visually inspected page images.**  
DOCX text extraction (or reading XML) will miss layout defects: clipping, overlap, missing glyphs, broken tables, spacing drift, and header/footer issues.

**Shipping gate:** before delivering any DOCX, you must:
- Run `render_docx.py` to produce `page-<N>.png` images (optionally also a PDF with `--emit_pdf`)

Found 10 relevant papers on 'What are the publication details and main methodological claims of Richard P. Gilliard's paper Fundamental units and constants of physics, especially its use of ct as a fourth-dimensional length coordinate?'.


1. Fundamental units and constants of physics
   2020 · Richard P. Gilliard · Advanced Studies in Theoretical Physics
   DOI: 10.12988/ASTP.2020.91466
   Abstract: It is generally believed that the most fundamental equations of physics require at least three units (length, mass, and time) and three fundamental constants (speed of light, gravitational constant, and Planck’s constant). In this work it is demonstrated that these equations can be rewritten such that the speed of light c and the unit of time t appear only as the product ct. As a result, the fundamental equations can be written in four dimensional format using only length and mass as units and with just two new constants (containing only those units) replacing the usual three. In addition Planck length and Planck mass are shown to be simple combinations of these two new constants. Similarly, the fine-structure constant is defined using these two constants instead of the usual three. The speed of light is only needed as the linear scale factor for the final conversion of fourth dimensional length to time.

2. The physical basis of natural units and truly fundamental constants
   2012 · Leon Hsu, Jong Ping Hsu · European Physical Journal Plus
   DOI: 10.1140/EPJP/I2012-12011-5
   Abstract: The natural unit system, in which the value of fundamental constants such as c and ℏ are set equal to one and all quantities are expressed in terms of a single unit, is usually introduced as a calculational convenience. However, we demonstrate that this system of natural units has a physical justification as well. We discuss and review the natural units, including definitions for each of the seven base units in the International System of Units (SI) in terms of a single unit. We also review the fundamental constants, which can be classified as units-dependent or units-independent. Units-independent constants, whose values are not determined by human conventions of units, may be interpreted as inherent constants of nature.

3. Physical Constants as Derived from Spatial-Causal Geometry (SCG) and the gamma(cause) Invariant
   2025
   DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.15042912
   Abstract: Physical Constants as Derived from Spatial–Causal Geometry (SCG) and the γ(cause) Invariant shows that the so-called fundamental constants of physics — G, c, h, α, k₍B₎, Λ, and H — are not independent inputs but equilibrium ratios that emerge from a single geometric field relation: a(x) = c² ∇lnρ(x) A universal closure ratio, the γ(cause) invariant, γ_cause = L/λ ≈ 1.216 provides the common geometric constraint linking curvature, propagation, and coherence across all scales. What this work contributes Unified geometric origin of seven constants from one field equation and closure invariant. Explicit SCG expressions for each constant, showing that constancy represents equilibrium, not assumption. Falsifiable predictions for density-linked variations and cross-constant constraints(e.g., H²/Λ ≈ 1/γ₍cause₎²). Experimental roadmap spanning laboratory interferometry, spectroscopy, lensing, and redshift surveys. Highlights G as a curvature–density equilibrium ratio; effective G varies with ρ(x) in extreme conditions. c as causal front speed depending on ρ(x):c_eff = c₀ √(ρ₀/ρ(x)). h from closure-normalized curvature energy:h = η c² γ_cause. α as nested photon geometry:α ≈ (r_photon/λ)ⁿ with r_photon/λ = 0.164 and n ≈ 2.73. k_B as curvature–entropy conversion:k_B = η_T c² γ_cause. Λ and H from first and second spatial derivatives of lnρ, connecting cosmic acceleration and apparent expansion. Keywords Spatial–Causal Geometryγ(cause) invariantfundamental constantsgeometric derivationcausal density fieldclosure ratiogravitational constant Gspeed of light cPlanck constant hfine-structure constant αBoltzmann constant k_Bcosmological constant ΛHubble parameter Hlensing time delaysinterferometryspectroscopyanisotropyunified physics 

4. Physical Constants and Geometry
   2025
   DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.16919124
   Abstract: <p>By definition, physical constants do not change. However, their conventional definitions often embed geometrical factors. For example, in Coulomb’s law the electrostatic constant includes a factor of 4π. Isaac Newton did the same with the gravitational constant by embedding the factor 4π. Einstein’s field equations incorporate the geometric factor through the term 8π G/c^4, rather than separating it from the constant. In this paper I argue that the gravitational constant should be freed from its geometrical contribution. This would improve consistency among fundamental interactions and clarify the distinction between geometry and physics in the definition of natural constants.</p> 

5. Why Constants Are Constants: A Chronos Field Explanation
   2025 · Hall Matthew
   DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.16283508
   Abstract: This paper presents a radical new framework explaining why the fundamental constants of physics—such as the speed of light (c), Planck’s constant (ℏ), the gravitational constant (G), and the fine-structure constant (α)—hold their seemingly arbitrary values. Through the Chronos Theory, time is treated not as a passive backdrop, but as a structured, oscillating field (τ) with curvature, feedback, and boundary dynamics. In this field-based model, physical constants are not inputs to equations but emergent, resonant harmonics stabilized by temporal geometry. The paper outlines how constants arise through curvature lock-in, energy density thresholds, and dimensional anchoring. It provides field equations, scaling relations, and testable predictions for future experimental validation—including potential drift in constants over time or under extreme conditions. This work reframes constants as byproducts of deeper time structure, unifying their origins across quantum, relativistic, and cosmological scales. 

6. "Deriving All Fundamental Physical Constants from a Unified Temporal Field Geometry"
   2025 · Anwar Morgan
   DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.15445914
   Abstract: This paper presents a novel derivation of all known fundamental physical constants from a unified temporal field geometry. Based on the hypothesis that time is the foundational field of the universe, we define a scalar temporal function , whose oscillations generate mass, energy, and interactions. Through precise mathematical analysis, we derive the values of , , , , , and Planck units from temporal dynamics alone, without relying on arbitrary assumptions. This approach offers a new foundation for unification in physics, linking quantum mechanics, relativity, and cosmology through a single time-based framework. 

7. Physical Constants and Geometry
   2025
   DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.16919123
   Abstract: By definition, physical constants do not change. However, their conventional definitions often embed geometrical factors. For example, in Coulomb’s law the electrostatic constant includes a factor of 4π. Isaac Newton did the same with the gravitational constant by embedding the factor 4π. Einstein’s field equations incorporate the geometric factor through the term 8π G/c^4, rather than separating it from the constant. In this paper I argue that the gravitational constant should be freed from its geometrical contribution. This would improve consistency among fundamental interactions and clarify the distinction between geometry and physics in the definition of natural constants. 

8. Deriving Physical Constants from Scalar Temporal Field Geometry
   2025 · Anwar Morgan
   DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.15623209
   Abstract: This paper presents a unified derivation of physical constants—specifically the speed of light and Planck’s constant —from the internal dynamics of a scalar temporal field . Without invoking any physical units or experimental parameters, the field is defined over a unitless lattice and governed by a classical wave equation derived from a standard Euler–Lagrange formulation. The propagation speed is shown to emerge from the ratio of spatial and temporal eigenfrequencies of the field’s modes, while the reduced Planck constant is derived as the ratio , where is the energy of a single oscillation mode and its angular frequency. The paper also includes a physical rescaling procedure using the known electron rest energy to map the dimensionless model to experimental values, recovering . This suggests that fundamental constants may arise as intrinsic geometric ratios within deeper field structures, independent of quantum postulates or dimensional assumptions. This work builds a bridge between classical field theory and quantum constants, supporting a broader theoretical program where the constants of nature emerge from internal geometric dynamics rather than being imposed externally. 

9. A New Dual System For The Fundamental Units, including and going beyond the newly revised SI
   2022 · Fayet, Pierre
   DOI: 10.48550/arxiv.1908.01584
   Abstract: We propose a new system for the fundamental units, which includes and goes beyond the present redefinition of the SI, by choosing also $c=\hbar=1$. By fixing $c=c_\circ $m/s = 1, $\hbar=\hbar_\circ $ Js = 1 and $\underline{μ_\circ}=μ_\circ $N/A$^2$ = 1, it allows us to define the metre, the joule, and the ampere as equal to (1/299 792 458) s, $(1/\hbar_\circ = .948 ... \times \ 10^{34})\ {\rm s}^{-1}$ and $\sqrt{μ_\circ \rm N}= \sqrt{μ_\circ c_\circ / \hbar_\circ}\ {\rm s}^{-1}= 1.890...\times 10^{18}\ {\rm s}^{-1}$. It presents at the same time the advantages and elegance of a system with $\hbar = c = \underline{μ_\circ} = \underline{ε_\circ } = k = N_A = 1\,$, where the vacuum magnetic permeability, electric permittivity, and impedance are all equal to 1. All units are rescaled from the natural ones and proportional to the s, s$^{-1}$, s$^{-2}$, ... or just 1, as for the coulomb, ohm and weber, now dimensionless. The coulomb is equal to $\sqrt{μ_\circ c_\circ / \hbar_\circ}= 1.890... \times 10^{18}$, and the elementary charge to $e=1.602...\times 10^{-19} {\rm C} = \sqrt{4πα}=.3028... $ . The ohm is equal to $1/μ_\circ c_\circ$ so that the impedance of the vacuum is $Z_\circ = 376.730... Ω=1$. The volt is $ 1/ \sqrt{μ_\circ c_\circ \hbar_\circ}\ {\rm s}^{-1} = 5.017... \times\ 10^{15}\ {\rm s}^{-1}$, and the tesla $c_\circ $V/m = $ \sqrt{{c_\circ^3}/{μ_\circ\hbar_\circ}}\ {\rm s}^{-2} = 4.509... \times 10^{32}\ {\rm s}^{-2}$. The weber is $ 1/ \sqrt{μ_\circ c_\circ \hbar_\circ} = 5.017... \times\ 10^{15}$. $\ K_J =483\,597. \ $... GHz/V $= e/π= $ .09639..., and $R_K = 25\,812.\ ...\ Ω=1/2α\simeq 68.518$. One can also fix $e$ = 1.602 176 634 $\times 10^{-19}$ C, at the price of adjusting the coulomb and all electrical units with $μ_\circ=4π\times 10^{-7}η^2$ where $η^2, \propto α$, is very close to 1. 

10. The Necessity of Absolute Space and Time for Light Speed Constancy: A Novel Experimental Approach to Fundamental Physics
   2025
   DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.17238425
   Abstract: This paper presents a theoretical framework arguing for the necessity of absolute space and time coordinates in defining the fundamental constant $c$ (speed of light). I propose that the Lorentz factor equation $\gamma = c \frac{dt}{ds}$ requires redefinition of $c$ in terms of absolute coordinates $c = \frac{ds_a}{dt_a}$, where the geometric field interval and absolute time provide the foundational framework for light's constant velocity. A novel experimental design is presented that avoids conventional time measurement devices and relies on simultaneity detection to verify light speed constancy. The proposed approach challenges current relativistic interpretations by asserting that absolute space-time must exist as the fundamental substrate that enables light to maintain constant velocity across all reference frames.

The coulomb is equal to $\sqrt{μ_\circ c_\circ / \hbar_\circ}= 1.890... \times 10^{18}$, and the elementary charge to $e=1.602...\times 10^{-19} {\rm C} = \sqrt{4πα}=.3028... $ . The ohm is equal to $1/μ_\circ c_\circ$ so that the impedance of the vacuum is $Z_\circ = 376.730... Ω=1$. The volt is $ 1/ \sqrt{μ_\circ c_\circ \hbar_\circ}\ {\rm s}^{-1} = 5.017... \times\ 10^{15}\ {\rm s}^{-1}$, and the tesla $c_\circ $V/m = $ \sqrt{{c_\circ^3}/{μ_\circ\hbar_\circ}}\ {\rm s}^{-2} = 4.509... \times 10^{32}\ {\rm s}^{-2}$. The weber is $ 1/ \sqrt{μ_\circ c_\circ \hbar_\circ} = 5.017... \times\ 10^{15}$. $\ K_J =483\,597. \ $... GHz/V $= e/π= $ .09639..., and $R_K = 25\,812.\ ...\ Ω=1/2α\simeq 68.518$. One can also fix $e$ = 1.602 176 634 $\times 10^{-19}$ C, at the price of adjusting the coulomb and all electrical units with $μ_\circ=4π\times 10^{-7}η^2$ where $η^2, \propto α$, is very close to 1.

papers.title: The Necessity of Absolute Space and Time for Light Speed Constancy: A Novel Experimental Approach to Fundamental Physics
papers.abstract: This paper presents a theoretical framework arguing for the necessity of absolute space and time coordinates in defining the fundamental constant $c$ (speed of light). I propose that the Lorentz factor equation $\gamma = c \frac{dt}{ds}$ requires redefinition of $c$ in terms of absolute coordinates $c = \frac{ds_a}{dt_a}$, where the geometric field interval and absolute time provide the foundational framework for light's constant velocity. A novel experimental design is presented that avoids conventional time measurement devices and relies on simultaneity detection to verify light speed constancy. The proposed approach challenges current relativistic interpretations by asserting that absolute space-time must exist as the fundamental substrate that enables light to maintain constant velocity across all reference frames.

bash -lc cat > /mnt/data/build_normalization_paper.py <<'PY'
from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Inches, Pt
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH
from docx.enum.table import WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT, WD_CELL_VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement
from docx.oxml.ns import qn
from docx.enum.section import WD_SECTION
from docx.enum.style import WD_STYLE_TYPE
from pathlib import Path

OUT = Path('/mnt/data')
docx_path = OUT/'Cross_Sector_Normalization_Audit_draft.docx'
md_path = OUT/'Cross_Sector_Normalization_Audit_draft.md'

TITLE = 'Deviation Is Data: A Cross-Sector Normalization Audit of Physical Equations'
SUBTITLE = 'A lossless stress test across classical, relativistic, quantum, transport, continuum, and control equations'

abstract = (
"We propose a cross-sector normalization audit for physical equations. The procedure fixes a common time-to-length coordinate, "
"w = ct, permits only declared invertible transformations, extracts any characteristic scales algebraically implied by each equation, "
"and then records what cannot be transformed away. The aim is not to make all laws look alike. It is to identify exactly which differences "
"are representational and which survive as residual structure. We demonstrate the procedure on a broad battery spanning kinematics, waves, "
"Newtonian mechanics, oscillators, electromagnetism, circuits, quantum mechanics, relativistic wave equations, transport, fluid mechanics, "
"kinetic theory, gravitation, cosmology, and deliberately awkward controls. The same base normalization yields coefficient balance in some propagative "
"systems, characteristic lengths or inverse lengths in many dynamical systems, dimensionless couplings in quantum and continuum problems, and persistent "
"operator-order, nonlinear, dissipative, discrete, source, signature, or topological residues in others. Static laws with no time coordinate are unchanged, "
"providing a useful negative control. No new physical law, value of a fundamental constant, or ontological interpretation is claimed. The proposed contribution "
"is methodological: the failure/survival map itself is the output. If a small fixed transformation grammar organizes a wide range of established physics and "
"its residual classes predict relations in equations not used to construct the grammar, that would constitute nontrivial representational compression."
)

sections = []
sections.append(("1. Introduction", [
"Dimensional analysis, natural units, similarity theory, and symmetry reduction are standard tools. Writing time as ct is standard in relativity; characteristic scales and dimensionless groups are standard throughout physics and engineering. The question considered here is therefore not whether any individual transformation is new. The question is whether these familiar operations become more informative when used as one fixed diagnostic across deliberately heterogeneous physical laws.",
"The proposed audit starts from a simple rule: normalize what can be normalized without loss, and keep an explicit ledger of what survives. The surviving structure is not treated as an inconvenience to be hidden by further ad hoc substitutions. It is the object of study. In this sense, deviation is data.",
"The procedure is intentionally agnostic about ontology. It does not claim that time is literally a spatial dimension, that spacetime is a material medium, or that equations reveal the substance of reality. It asks a narrower representational question: after a common, invertible normalization, how much of the apparent diversity among physical equations is scale or notation, and how much remains as irreducible mathematical structure?"
]))

sections.append(("2. The audit protocol", [
"2.1 Frozen base normalization. Introduce a length-valued temporal coordinate w = kt. For a trajectory v = dx/dt, this gives dx/dw = v/k. The calibration k = c makes a c-propagating trajectory satisfy dx/dw = 1. Once calibrated, k is frozen at c across the battery; it is not re-fit equation by equation.",
"2.2 Derivative rule. Because w = ct, ∂/∂t = c ∂/∂w and ∂²/∂t² = c² ∂²/∂w². More generally, each nth time derivative contributes c^n. A change of units can alter coefficients, but it cannot by itself change the order or algebraic type of an operator. Thus a first-order-in-time diffusion law does not become a second-order wave equation merely by writing time in length units.",
"2.3 Allowed secondary transformations. Additional rescalings are permitted only when they are invertible, explicitly declared, and either universal (for example, B̃ = cB in vacuum Maxwell theory or U = u/c for a velocity field) or algebraically forced by coefficients already present in the equation. A characteristic scale may be extracted, but it is recorded before being scaled out. No empirical parameter is fitted merely to improve the appearance of a result.",
"2.4 Canonicalization and residual ledger. After the base normalization, the equation is reduced to the simplest dimensionless or geometrized form available under the allowed transformations. The remaining information is classified as one or more residuals: characteristic scale, dimensionless coupling, operator-order mismatch, metric/signature structure, nonlinearity, dissipation, dispersion, finite/discrete scale, source term, boundary or topological condition, or absence of a temporal variable.",
"2.5 Failure criterion. The method earns value only if the same small grammar remains useful across heterogeneous sectors. If every equation demands its own discretionary transformation, the exercise reduces to ordinary problem-specific nondimensionalization. If residuals repeatedly fall into a small number of stable classes, the procedure provides representational compression. A stronger test is out-of-sample: a residual relation inferred in one family should organize or predict a relation in a law not used to construct it."
]))

sections.append(("3. Positive calibrators", [
"The first examples are not evidence of new physics; they calibrate the procedure against equations already known to privilege c.",
"Velocity: v = dx/dt becomes β = dx/dw = v/c. A light trajectory has β = 1.",
"Generic wave equation: ∂²_t ψ = u²∇²ψ becomes ∂²_w ψ = (u/c)²∇²ψ. For u = c, the coefficients of the temporal-length and spatial second derivatives are equal. The remaining Lorentzian sign appears when the equation is written as a quadratic operator and is not erased by this normalization.",
"Vacuum Maxwell equations become especially transparent if B̃ = cB: ∇·E = 0, ∇·B̃ = 0, ∂_w E = ∇×B̃, and ∂_w B̃ = -∇×E. This is a coefficient-balanced first-order system. The result is a standard reformulation, used here only as a positive control."
]))

sections.append(("4. Representative results", [
"The stress test does not collapse all equations into a single form. Instead, it repeatedly converts temporal rates into inverse lengths, transport coefficients into lengths, accelerations into curvature-like quantities, and relativistic mass terms into inverse Compton lengths. Other distinctions survive exactly as expected.",
"Classical mechanics. Newton's law m x¨ = F becomes x_ww = F/(mc²). Harmonic recurrence produces the length ℓ_ω = c/ω. Damping adds an inverse length γ/c while preserving the damping ratio γ/ω. The nonlinear pendulum reduces to θ_WW + sin θ = 0 after scaling by ℓ = c√(L/g); the finite-angle residue sin θ - θ cannot be removed by the base normalization.",
"Quantum mechanics. The free Schrödinger equation becomes i∂_w ψ = -(λ̄_C/2)∇²ψ, exposing λ̄_C = ħ/(mc). A general potential enters as V/(ħc), an inverse-length field. Hydrogen leaves the fine-structure constant α as a dimensionless coupling after the electron Compton scale is removed. The Klein-Gordon and Dirac equations likewise expose the inverse reduced Compton wavelength as their mass scale while retaining Lorentzian/gamma-matrix structure.",
"Transport and continuum mechanics. Advection balances cleanly when U = u/c: ∂_w φ + U·∇φ = 0. Diffusion does not: ∂_w T = (D/c)∇²T, retaining a first-versus-second derivative-order distinction and the diffusion length D/c. Navier-Stokes, after u = cU and p = ρc²Π, becomes U_w + (U·∇)U = -∇Π + (ν/c)∇²U + f/c². The residual viscosity length ν/c is real bookkeeping, not a failure to normalize.",
"Gravity. Newtonian Kepler dynamics produces the gravitational length GM/c². Coulomb attraction produces qQ/(4πε₀mc²); both then reduce to the same inverse-square dimensionless central-force equation after their sector-specific lengths are scaled out. This identifies an equivalence class without implying that the interactions are physically identical. General relativity is already geometrized: the Einstein equation retains curvature, metric signature, Λ, and the conversion G/c⁴. The audit therefore adds little to its covariant form and records that fact."
]))

sections.append(("5. Deliberately awkward controls", [
"A useful diagnostic must include equations selected because they should not collapse into the positive-control pattern.",
"Diffusion and radioactive decay retain first-order temporal evolution. Korteweg-de Vries retains mixed first- and third-order derivatives together with nonlinear and dispersive coefficients. Boltzmann retains a phase-space collision operator. Navier-Stokes retains nonlinear advection and dissipation. These are informative partial controls: w = ct reorganizes their coefficients but does not erase their mathematical type.",
"Stronger negative controls contain no time variable at all. The ideal-gas law PV = Nk_BT, the first law dU = TdS - p dV + μ dN, Boltzmann's entropy S = k_B ln Ω, Hooke's static law F = -kx, Laplace/Poisson equations, and static constitutive relations are unchanged by the base temporal transformation. The procedure therefore does not manufacture a fourth-coordinate structure where none appears in the law. Such equations can still be included at the later scale/invariant stage, but they are correctly classified as temporally silent under the base audit."
]))

sections.append(("6. What the battery shows", [
"Across the examples, the most common conversion rules are simple: a rate ω becomes an inverse length ω/c; a time τ becomes a length cτ; diffusivity or kinematic viscosity becomes D/c or ν/c; ħ/m becomes the reduced Compton length ħ/(mc); GM becomes GM/c²; and an acceleration becomes a/c². These are largely familiar geometrized-unit identities.",
"The informative output is not those identities themselves but the residual pattern. Second-order propagation laws can coefficient-balance when their characteristic speed is c; slower wave systems retain u/c. First-order irreversible laws retain their derivative-order asymmetry. Quantum equations retain mass scales and dimensionless couplings. Continuum equations retain transport lengths and nonlinear groups. Discrete systems retain finite-spacing functions such as sin(qa/2)/(qa/2). Covariant relativistic laws retain signature and curvature. Static laws remain static.",
"The working conjecture is therefore modest: a common lossless normalization may provide a useful cross-sector coordinate system for classifying physical equations by what survives it. The classification is falsifiable in the practical sense that it can fail to compress: a sufficiently heterogeneous battery may reveal that the residual vocabulary proliferates without bound or that the allowed transformations require continual discretionary retuning."
]))

sections.append(("7. Relation to prior work", [
"The component techniques have substantial prior art. Buckingham dimensional analysis and Bridgman's dimensional analysis formalized unit-invariant groups and similitude. Wolsky explicitly examined uniform length/time scale changes across classical mechanics, nonrelativistic quantum mechanics, and relativistic quantum field theory. Natural-unit and geometrized-unit methods routinely set c = 1 or use ct as a length coordinate. Gilliard explicitly rewrote fundamental equations so that c and t appear through ct and treated c as the conversion between fourth-dimensional length and time.",
"Similarity and equivalence-transform methods provide a more formal mathematical neighborhood; Lie-symmetry methods can algorithmically nondimensionalize differential equations and identify invariant coordinates. Recent data-driven work uses Buckingham-Pi constraints to discover dimensionless groups and governing laws from data.",
"Mukohyama and Uzan provide especially relevant but distinct prior art for a different question: they begin with a positive-definite four-dimensional metric and introduce a scalar clock field whose gradient selects a local time direction; field-dependent couplings are then chosen so that scalar, vector, spinor, and point-particle sectors acquire effective Lorentzian dynamics. Their program is a constructive Euclidean-to-Lorentzian mechanism. The present audit does not introduce a clock field or modify the physical content of the equations; it begins with established equations and asks what a fixed, lossless normalization removes or leaves behind.",
"Accordingly, no novelty claim is made here for ct coordinates, natural units, nondimensionalization, similarity theory, or rank-one Lorentzian constructions. The proposed contribution is the cross-sector protocol in which a frozen base normalization is applied broadly, residuals are treated as the primary output, deliberately non-collapsing controls are included, and success is judged by compression and out-of-sample organization rather than by the ability to rewrite any single equation."
]))

sections.append(("8. Limits and falsifiable next steps", [
"First, a coordinate rewrite is not a derivation of new dynamics. In particular, w = ct does not by itself produce the Minkowski metric, Lorentz factor, quantum mechanics, or any measured constant. Whenever a metric, constitutive relation, boundary condition, or approximation is added, that addition must be recorded separately.",
"Second, 'representational' is always relative to the declared transformation class. A residual that survives the present audit might disappear under a broader admissible equivalence group. The protocol therefore requires an explicit transformation ledger rather than a metaphysical distinction between appearance and reality.",
"Third, a useful next phase is computational. Freeze the transformation rules in software, feed in a preregistered battery of equations from unrelated sectors, and automatically output the normalized form, generated characteristic scales, dimensionless groups, operator-order pattern, and residual class. A blinded holdout set should be reserved. The method becomes scientifically interesting only if the residual taxonomy remains small and stable, or if relations inferred from the training battery organize the holdouts without additional fitting.",
"The strongest possible result would not be 'all physics is the same equation.' It would be a much narrower claim: after conventional unit freedom and known equivalence transformations are factored out, a surprisingly small residual vocabulary may suffice to describe how major classes of physical law differ."
]))

sections.append(("9. Conclusion", [
"A common time-to-length normalization is mathematically elementary. Used as a one-off substitution, it is mostly a familiar change of units. Used as a frozen cross-sector audit, however, it provides a disciplined question: what disappears, what survives, and do the survivors recur in a small number of forms?",
"The demonstrations in this paper show both positive and negative behavior. Some propagation systems become coefficient-balanced; many equations expose natural length scales or dimensionless couplings; dissipative, nonlinear, discrete, source-driven, and static laws preserve exactly the distinctions one would expect them to preserve. That is the desired behavior. The audit is not designed to make every equation fit. It is designed to turn the pattern of fit and non-fit into structured data.",
"The next test is therefore breadth, automation, and holdout prediction—not interpretive escalation."
]))

# footer/page number via simple field

thoughts.summary: Drafted and audited the cross-sector normalization paper document

parts:
Yes. I turned it into a standalone methodology paper rather than an SAT/H(s)H paper, so the central claim has to stand or fall independently.

The core is exactly the rule we just converged on: use a frozen, lossless normalization across heterogeneous laws, record whatever survives rather than forcing it away, and treat systematic deviation as the experimental output. fileciteturn92file0L1022-L1040 I also kept the stricter bookkeeping rules from the working note: invertible transformations only, no equation-by-equation retuning, and explicit retention of irreducible residues. fileciteturn92file0L130-L143

The draft is only eight pages despite having a **50-equation stress-test appendix**. It includes positive calibrators, partial failures, and deliberately obnoxious controls: diffusion, decay, KdV, Boltzmann, Navier-Stokes, static Poisson/Laplace, ideal gas, first law, entropy, static Hooke law, etc. It also includes Schrödinger, hydrogen, Klein-Gordon, Dirac, Maxwell, circuits, oscillators, Kepler/Coulomb, geodesics, Einstein/Friedmann, transport and fluid equations.

I deliberately made the novelty claim conservative: \(ct\), natural units, nondimensionalization, similarity theory, and Euclidean-to-Lorentzian constructions are all acknowledged as prior art. The proposed contribution is the **cross-sector residual audit**, including negative controls and the requirement that usefulness be judged by compression and holdout performance.

[Download the Word manuscript](sandbox:/mnt/data/Cross_Sector_Normalization_Audit_draft.docx)

[Download the Markdown source](sandbox:/mnt/data/Cross_Sector_Normalization_Audit_draft.md)

The working title is **“Deviation Is Data: A Cross-Sector Normalization Audit of Physical Equations.”** I think that captures the actual move much better than framing it around dimensional symmetry alone.
